questions.prompt: Groups helping Democrats have spent $52.7M in the ME Senate race. Are Democrats playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Democrats here is offense.

questions.prompt: HMP (a super PAC) has spent $11.3M in NC's 1st District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: A hybrid PAC can do what a super PAC can't. What?
options: Give directly to candidates from a limited account
questions.why: A hybrid PAC keeps two accounts: a limited one for contributions to candidates and an unlimited one for independent spending.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
In the NH Senate race, outside money favors Republicans by $23.4M. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Democrat leads fundraising by $18.5M.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Democrats have spent $2.0M in LA's 6th District House race. Are Democrats playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Democrats hold this seat now, so money helping Democrats here is defense.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
Can a super PAC give $10,000 directly to a House candidate's campaign?
questions.why: Super PACs can raise unlimited money but can't give to candidates or coordinate with them. They can only spend independently.

questions.prompt: NRCC (a party committee) has spent $1.9M in NM's 2nd District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: A party's coordinated spending in the last three weeks before Nov. 3 is disclosed when?
questions.why: Coordinated spending appears only on regular reports. Anything after Oct. 14 lands on the post-general report, due Dec. 3.
